channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Middle East conflict threatens Kenya's $32.8m tea exports
item.description: Kenya’s tea industry is confronting a new wave of uncertainty as escalating conflict in the Middle East threatens vital export routes and a market that bought $32.8 million (KSh4.26 billion) worth of Kenyan tea in 2024.

item.title: U.S. Embassy cancels visa appointments, issues security alert in Nigeria amid potential protests
item.description: The U.S. Embassy in Nigeria has canceled all visa appointments scheduled for Wednesday, March 4, 2026, citing security concerns over potential protests linked to the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran.

item.title: “No one dares touch Egypt,” El Sisi assures his people, amidst concerns of war
item.description: Anxiety in the Middle East over the Israel/Iran war has found its way to Egypt, an African country that has a long and uncomfortable history with Israel.

item.title: Bezos and Gates-backed firm fights for DRC’s mineral data in exchange for more investments
item.description: The dispute between the US mining firm, Kobold Metals, backed by billionaires Jeff Bezos and Bill Gates, and Belgium's AfricaMuseum over the digitization of colonial-era maps of what is now the Democratic Republic of the Congo may be intensifying.

item.title: Top 5 African countries most dependent on tourism (Share of GDP)
item.description: Tourism remains a major economic engine across Africa, but in some countries, it is especially critical, contributing a significant share of national GDP and ranking among the most tourism-dependent economies globally.

item.title: Africa’s premier BRICS member again offers to play big brother to major warring states
item.description: South Africa, similar to its move last year, has yet again offered to be a mediator in a major global conflict, this time between Israel and Iran.

item.title: Fastest African economies to hit $100 billion GDP since independence
item.description: Africa’s economies have been on quite the rollercoaster since independence, and hitting the $100 billion GDP mark tells some interesting stories. Some countries sprinted to the milestone, while others took the scenic route.

item.title: German shipping giant suspends Africa–Upper Gulf cargo amid rising Iran tensions
item.description: German-based Hapag-Lloyd, one of the world’s largest container shipping companies, has suspended cargo bookings from Africa to the Upper Gulf region, citing heightened operational and security risks.

item.title: How a China-funded survey uncovered $3B in new mineral deposits in Liberia
item.description: A China-funded national mineral resource survey has revealed significant new mineral deposits in Liberia, offering fresh opportunities for economic growth and investment.

item.title: Ghana strikes visa waiver agreement with another Caribbean nation
item.description: Ghana has signed a visa waiver agreement with the Caribbean nation of Saint Kitts and Nevis that allows holders of ordinary passports to travel between the two countries without visas.
